theme: Oh, how abundant is your goodness
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 31:19-24. This is the second half of the psalm you read on Day 619. After the trouble, the singer turns to thanks. Read it with the verses 1 to 18 fresh in your mind.
settingTheScene: The first half of Psalm 31 was a prayer in the middle of distress. These closing verses look back from the other side. David has been heard, and he reflects on the goodness of God that is stored up for those who trust him. He ends by calling all God’s people to love him and take courage.
observation: “stored up for those who fear you” (v. 19).
“In the cover of your presence you hide them from the plots of men” (v. 20).
“he has wondrously shown his steadfast love to me when I was in a besieged city” (v. 21).
“I had said in my alarm, I am cut off from your sight” (v. 22).
“you heard the voice of my pleas for mercy” (v. 22).
“Love the LORD, all you his saints!” (v. 23).
“Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all who wait for the LORD!” (v. 24).
interpretation:
Verse 19 is an exclamation: “Oh, how abundant is your goodness!” David is overwhelmed. The goodness of God is not scarce, and it is stored up, like treasure in a storehouse, for those who fear him and take refuge in him. It is given “in the sight of the children of mankind,” so that others can see.

Verse 20 describes how it is delivered. God hides his people “in the cover of your presence” from the plots of men and “in your shelter from the strife of tongues.” David had been slandered (see verse 13), and he knows that God’s nearness is the safest place.

In verse 21, he blesses the LORD for showing steadfast love in a “besieged city.” He had felt trapped, surrounded, and helpless. Then he admits, “I had said in my alarm, I am cut off from your sight.” This is the honest confession of a believer who felt abandoned. But he was not. “You heard the voice of my pleas for mercy when I cried to you for help.” What he felt in alarm was not the truth. God had been listening all along.

Then David turns outward. “Love the LORD, all you his saints!” He has learned something he wants others to know. The LORD preserves the faithful, and abundantly repays the proud. And the last words are an encouragement: “Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all who wait for the LORD.”

Read this beside Luke 19 to 21. Jesus entered a besieged city in the week of his death. He felt the plots of men. Yet he was not cut off, and the Father vindicated him. And because of the cross, the goodness stored up for those who take refuge in God is ours.
connection: Psalm 27:13-14 ends with almost the same call to wait and take courage. Psalm 34:8-10 says to taste and see that the LORD is good. Isaiah 64:4 and 1 Corinthians 2:9 speak of what God has prepared for those who wait for him. Romans 8:35-39 says nothing can separate us from the love of God. Ephesians 1:3 says he has blessed us with every spiritual blessing. Jonah 2:4 echoes the feeling of being cast out from his sight.
application:
Make a list of the goodness God has stored up and given you. Thank him for each one.

Remember a time you felt cut off from God and he was close. Write it down.

Tell a friend, as David does: love the LORD.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for goodness he has stored up for those who fear him.
Thank him for hiding you in the cover of his presence.
Ask him to make you strong and take heart.
